verdict.rationale: SES documents leasing dedicated IPs reserved for exclusive use. Its managed dedicated IPs are set up automatically and "automatically warm up for each ISP individually and auto-scale based on your sending volume," which satisfies the automated ramp-up option of the story. One community comment says SES offers no dedicated IPs, but it comes from an old thread, is contradicted by current first-party docs, and reports no hands-on failure, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that managed warmup works, and documented warmup details (schedule or ramp guidance) for standard, non-managed dedicated IPs.

support.subject: As a deliverability manager, I can get dedicated IPs with documented warmup — automated ramp-up or a published warmup schedule — when my volume outgrows shared pools

citations.quote: You can also use dedicated IP addresses that are reserved for your exclusive use by leasing them for an additional cost. This gives you complete control over your sender reputation.
they automatically warm up for each ISP individually and auto-scale based on your sending volume.
